discovered_real_problems: High-frequency heartbeat itself can become information waste if every pulse writes durable logs.
A pending formal C packet existed while the existing C task was disabled; scheduler liveness is still a real failure mode.
Restart/catch-up must be bounded or missed windows can create a burst that duplicates work.
Pulse identity and event cursor must be persisted or restart can replay old work.
Online/Local concurrent writers need a single-writer or compare-and-swap/lease rule to prevent state races.
Endpoint outage notifications need dedupe/cooldown or failure reporting itself becomes waste.

cloud_fallback.constraint: scheduled workflow must exist on default branch and can be delayed/dropped under load

why_not_live_yet: Owner Windows Small-Nest/Tower package has not yet produced real owner-machine evidence and no separately authorized always-on cloud runner is currently active.
